text:
Anya: Hey team — OrbitEdge contract review: they want per-device hourly snapshots AND a daily aggregated file for billing. Proposal: Redwood accepts canonical event stream, performs local hourly fan-out into partner-facing hourly snapshots (signed), and we run a 24h reconciliation window to surface deltas. Thoughts?
Matt: Do we have clarity on whether billing will use partner snapshots or our canonical aggregates? That affects who is authoritative for disputes.
Gwen: Partner expects their hourly snapshot to be the source of truth for their customers. They still want Redwood to keep canonical events for audit. They also want a 9am UTC daily reconciliation csv.
Ranjit: Ok — plan sounds feasible. Implementation notes: 1) Ingest events as we do now; 2) Produce partner_hourly_snapshot table per tz-normalized hour; 3) Expose a signed S3 file (or HTTP push) + a reconciliation API that accepts partner deltas. Keep 24h window for late-arrivals.
Sofia: Two engineering constraints: idempotency + signature verification. We should require event_id on each raw event and HMAC header for snapshot callbacks. Also need to bound memory for hourly fan-out (streaming write to S3 rather than buffering).
Ranjit: Example webhook payload (hourly snapshot):
```json
{
  "snapshot_hour": "2026-03-21T14:00:00Z",
  "region": "eu-west-1",
  "device_rows": [
    { "device_id": "orb-00123", "usage_units": 1234, "meter_type": "tokens" },
    { "device_id": "orb-00456", "usage_units": 0, "meter_type": "tokens" }
  ],
  "snapshot_id": "snap_20260321_14_euw1_0001"
}
```
Sofia: Signature header example: `X-Redwood-Signature: v1=HEX_HMAC_SHA256(body, key)` and we validate within the webhook handler. For ingestion events we also require `event_id` and `event_ts`.
Matt: For billing correctness we need a reconciliation SQL snippet to diff partner snapshot vs ours. Rough draft:
```sql
SELECT p.device_id, p.usage_units as partner_units, r.usage_units as redwood_units, (p.usage_units - r.usage_units) as delta
FROM partner_hourly p
LEFT JOIN redwood_hourly r ON p.device_id = r.device_id AND p.snapshot_hour = r.snapshot_hour
WHERE abs(p.usage_units - coalesce(r.usage_units,0)) > 0
```
Gwen: Partner also wants timezone handling docs — they report local tz per device but billing will be UTC hour buckets. We should publish a small spec.
Anya: Action items: 1) Ranjit/Sofia — finalize webhook + signing & streaming S3 writer (due Mar 28) ; 2) Matt — define reconciliation thresholds & dispute policy (due Mar 30) ; 3) Gwen — confirm partner S3 vs push preference and sample files (due Mar 26) ; 4) Anya — draft partner-facing spec and runbook (due Apr 1).
Ranjit: I'll add an extra audit column `ingest_received_ts` and keep raw_event_payload for 30 days to support audits. Also implementing per-hour file rolling to avoid large objects.
Sofia: FYI for infra: please avoid using single large aggregator container; we'll shard by region for snapshot generation.
ingest-bot: TEST: forwarded hourly snapshot to orbitedge-dev (200 OK) — snapshot_id=snap_20260321_14_euw1_0001
Matt: Can we add a small tolerance for clock skew (±2 minutes) when assigning events to hour buckets? Partners often have device clocks off.
Ranjit: Yes — will floor/ceil with a 2-minute grace window; events landing inside grace window will be assigned to nearest hour and flagged.
Gwen: Partner asks: how will we handle late-arrival credits? They want a single daily delta file and a manual dispute path.
Anya: We'll include late-arrival deltas in the 9am UTC reconciliation and expose a dispute endpoint. Matt — please outline dispute SLA in your doc.
Sofia: Devops note: we should include a synthetic end-to-end test that runs nightly in staging and validates sample files, signatures, and reconciliation job output. I'll add this to the CI matrix.
Anya: Great — I'll collect these into a partner spec and ping legal for contract clause around 24h reconciliation. Thanks everyone. :raised_hands:
